assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning (a probe)

The scenario needs the session to stay working past its turn's own end while a backgrounded shell process lives. Agent side: OpenCode 2.x can move a running shell tool into background observation (POST /api/session/{id}/background, 2.1.4 openapi.json). Daemon side, read from code: BackgroundProcessCount is set only by the shared tailer (tailer_metrics.go) and the muse/geminicli parsers; the opencode fold (metrics.go, metrics_v2.go) bypasses the tailer and never sets it, so nothing holds a 2.x session working after its turn ends. The probe records the shape to confirm that.

## Spec choices

The scenario's: the session's ready comes well after the turn's own Stop hook (held while the process lives).
caveats: Expected to fail (daemon incapable, by code); the probe recording is the evidence for the freeze.

sources.note: queryV2SessionMetrics re-folds every session_message row in seq order; cumulative tokens/cost come from the session_v2 columns
BackgroundProcessCount is set by the tailer; the opencode fold never runs it

preconditions: One OpenCode 2.x `serve --service` running, with a model it can reach (this host: the sandbox service, local Kolibri-1 4-bit model (mlx_lm) at 127.0.0.1:8087); the rig never starts, stops or reconfigures it
The three XDG exports, coexist IRRLICHT_ONBOARD_HOME and a non-7837 bind address from replaydata/agents/opencode-v2/prerequisites.md; OPENCODE_DB unset
setup: driver-interactive.sh (API driver) refuses before creating anything unless exactly one `serve --service` runs, its environment carries the run's XDG_* values, and the plugin's beacon resolves this run's daemon

It creates one session over POST /api/session at <staging>/cwd, waits for the service log to show the plugin the daemon installed loading for that location with no load failure, then drives the script; the session's session_message rows are exported read-only as the transcript
send a prompt that runs `sleep 25`; once the shell tool runs, background it; wait for the turn end; 30s

script.text: Run the shell command `sleep 25` with the shell tool, then reply with exactly the word: started.

verify: the turn ends while the backgrounded shell process still runs
the session stays working until the process exits
